correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact polar-area density, integrates the horizontal fiber of the affine Funk ball, differentiates an analytic one-dimensional integral, and obtains three closed Hessian entries. The optimized curvature is their Schur complement. Its numerator is a positive quadratic in \(A=\operatorname{artanh}\lambda\); both roots are below \(\lambda\), while \(A>\lambda\). A packaged numerical verifier independently checks the integral/Hessian formulas at representative radii, but the universal sign is established analytically.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-finding corpus searches, the current own ledger, and the two directly relevant public primary texts were compared at the level of statements and implications. The 2020 paper supplies the finite-radius functional and unconditional-body results; the 2023 paper supplies finite-center uniqueness and an asymptotic regular-polygon extremum. Neither gives a finite-radius trapezoid Hessian, and neither implication yields the all-radius negative Schur complement computed here.
residual_risks: A cited in-preparation work on the Blaschke metric/centro-projective volume is not a verified public source and could not be used for coverage comparison.
The literature search cannot prove absolute novelty; an independently phrased local Hessian computation could exist outside the indexed and directly inspected sources.

value.rationale: The parameter \(\delta\) is the complete affine modulus of trapezoids, so this is not an arbitrary coordinate slice. The result gives an exact all-finite-radius local stability law at the affine-regular quadrilateral, including the motion of the optimizing center and the transverse curvature. It directly links the finite-radius Funk functional introduced in 2020 with the later large-radius regular-polygon extremum, while explicitly showing how the center response interpolates between the ordinary and infinite-radius Santaló limits.
